## Solution

**Setup.** Place the square base in the $xyz$-coordinate system:
$$A=(0,0,0),\quad B=(5,0,0),\quad C=(5,5,0),\quad D=(0,5,0).$$
The center of the base is $O=(2.5,2.5,0)$, so the apex is $V=(2.5,\,2.5,\,10\sqrt2)$.

**Determining the cutting plane.** The plane passes through $A$ and is parallel to diagonal $BD$, whose direction is $(-1,1,0)$. Hence the normal $\mathbf{n}=(a,b,c)$ satisfies $\mathbf{n}\cdot(-1,1,0)=0$, giving $a=b$. Write $\mathbf{n}=(a,a,c)$.

The plane passes through the origin, so its equation is $ax+ay+cz=0$.

The angle between line $AB$ (direction $(1,0,0)$) and the plane is $30°$, so
$$\sin 30°=\frac{|\mathbf{n}\cdot(1,0,0)|}{\|\mathbf{n}\|}=\frac{|a|}{\sqrt{2a^2+c^2}}=\frac12.$$
Squaring: $\frac{a^2}{2a^2+c^2}=\frac14\Rightarrow 4a^2=2a^2+c^2\Rightarrow c^2=2a^2$, so $c=\pm a\sqrt2$.

Taking $a=1$: $\mathbf{n}=(1,1,\sqrt2)$ or $\mathbf{n}=(1,1,-\sqrt2)$.

- Plane $x+y+\sqrt2\,z=0$: evaluating at $V$ gives $5+20=25>0$, and at $B,C,D$ all positive — only $A$ lies on the plane, giving a degenerate section. **Rejected.**
- Plane $x+y-\sqrt2\,z=0$: at $V$ we get $5-20=-15<0$, while $B,C,D$ give positive values. This separates $V$ from $B,C,D$ with $A$ on the plane. **Accepted.**

**Verification of conditions.** Normal $\mathbf{n}=(1,1,-\sqrt2)$: $\mathbf{n}\cdot(-1,1,0)=0$ (parallel to $BD$ ✓); $\sin\theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+1+2}}=\frac12\Rightarrow\theta=30°$ ✓; $A$ satisfies $0=0$ ✓.

**Finding the section vertices.** Evaluate $f(x,y,z)=x+y-\sqrt2\,z$ at each vertex:
$$f(A)=0,\; f(B)=5>0,\; f(C)=10>0,\; f(D)=5>0,\; f(V)=-15<0.$$

The plane crosses edges $VB$, $VC$, $VD$ (sign changes) and passes through $A$. No base edge other than at $A$ is crossed (at $z=0$ the plane is $x+y=0$, touching the base only at $A$).

**Edge $VB$:** $P=V+t(B-V)=\bigl(\tfrac52(1+t),\;\tfrac52(1-t),\;10\sqrt2(1-t)\bigr)$.
$$f=5-20(1-t)=-15+20t=0\;\Rightarrow\;t=\tfrac34.$$
$$P_{VB}=\left(\tfrac{35}{8},\;\tfrac{5}{8},\;\tfrac{5\sqrt2}{2}\right).$$

**Edge $VC$:** $P=V+t(C-V)=\bigl(\tfrac52(1+t),\;\tfrac52(1+t),\;10\sqrt2(1-t)\bigr)$.
$$f=5(1+t)-20(1-t)=-15+25t=0\;\Rightarrow\;t=\tfrac35.$$
$$P_{VC}=(4,\;4,\;4\sqrt2).$$

**Edge $VD$:** $P=V+t(D-V)=\bigl(\tfrac52(1-t),\;\tfrac52(1+t),\;10\sqrt2(1-t)\bigr)$.
$$f=5-20(1-t)=-15+20t=0\;\Rightarrow\;t=\tfrac34.$$
$$P_{VD}=\left(\tfrac{5}{8},\;\tfrac{35}{8},\;\tfrac{5\sqrt2}{2}\right).$$

The section is the quadrilateral $A\,P_{VB}\,P_{VC}\,P_{VD}$.

**Computing the area.** Since the plane passes through the origin, the area of a planar polygon with vertices $P_1,\dots,P_n$ (ordered) is
$$\text{Area}=\tfrac12\left|\sum_{i} P_i\times P_{i+1}\right|.$$

With $P_1=A=(0,0,0)$, the terms $P_1\times P_2$ and $P_4\times P_1$ vanish. We need $P_2\times P_3 + P_3\times P_4$:

$$P_2\times P_3=\left(\tfrac{35}{8},\tfrac{5}{8},\tfrac{5\sqrt2}{2}\right)\times(4,4,4\sqrt2)=\left(-\tfrac{15\sqrt2}{2},\;-\tfrac{15\sqrt2}{2},\;15\right).$$

$$P_3\times P_4=(4,4,4\sqrt2)\times\left(\tfrac{5}{8},\tfrac{35}{8},\tfrac{5\sqrt2}{2}\right)=\left(-\tfrac{15\sqrt2}{2},\;-\tfrac{15\sqrt2}{2},\;15\right).$$

$$\text{Sum}=\left(-15\sqrt2,\;-15\sqrt2,\;30\right),\qquad|\text{Sum}|=\sqrt{450+450+900}=\sqrt{1800}=30\sqrt2.$$

$$\boxed{\text{Area}=\tfrac12\cdot 30\sqrt2=15\sqrt2.}$$

**Cross-check via diagonals.** Diagonals $\overrightarrow{AP_{VC}}=(4,4,4\sqrt2)$ and $\overrightarrow{P_{VB}P_{VD}}=\left(-\tfrac{15}{4},\tfrac{15}{4},0\right)$:
$$\mathbf{d}_1\times\mathbf{d}_2=(-15\sqrt2,\,-15\sqrt2,\,30),\quad |\mathbf{d}_1\times\mathbf{d}_2|=30\sqrt2,\quad \text{Area}=\tfrac12\cdot 30\sqrt2=15\sqrt2.\;\checkmark$$
